Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals Amid Abnormally High Contract Exchange Rates

According to Unchained, Ethereum staking protocol Swell has paused deposits and withdrawals for swETH and rswETH until it corrects the net asset values (NAV) and exchange rates of both tokens. Data shows that the swETH and rswETH contracts reported exchange rates of approximately 1.203 ETH and 1.138 ETH, respectively, about 6% and 5% higher than normal levels.

On-chain analyst Spreek suspected a compromise of the relevant token admin keys and identified a malicious upgrade contract that could potentially impact around 2,500 ETH, though the upgrade has not yet been executed. Swell stated that no ETH has been transferred out of the affected contracts and that the exact cause remains under investigation. — link

Keystone Confirms Customer Data Exposure Following Unauthorized Website Access

Keystone Hardware Wallet confirmed that a third party obtained customer shipping and order information following unauthorized access to its official website. The incident was detected on October 20, with the data exposure confirmed on October 23 after reviewing API activity with Shopify. Exposed information included names, contact details, shipping addresses, purchased items, and prices. Payment card and bank details, recovery phrases, private keys, and wallet passwords were not exposed. Keystone said it has blocked the access, fixed the vulnerability, and is notifying affected customers. It also warned of impersonation scams involving fake refunds, replacement devices, or order fixes. — link

Jeff Yan: Hyperliquid Is More Like the Internet or Linux Than a Traditional Exchange

Hyperliquid Labs co-founder Jeff Yan said at DAS Asia 2026 on October 7 that Hyperliquid should not simply be viewed as a competitor to any particular exchange. He noted that Hyperliquid was initially compared to DeFi protocols, then major crypto exchanges, and now even traditional giants like CME and Nasdaq, yet none is a perfect comparison. Yan argued that Hyperliquid is more like the internet or Linux, providing neutral public infrastructure rather than building multiple systems that serve the same purpose. He emphasized that the Hyperliquid community is not trying to replace existing platforms, but hopes to empower them with technology that helps them better serve their users. — link

According to the Financial Times, the Bank of Israel publicly rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s proposal to use cryptocurrencies to circumvent potential international financial sanctions. On October 24, the central bank stated that crypto could not serve as a means of bypassing sanctions, urging the government to preserve economic ties with major trading partners and prevent further restrictions. In an October 23 television interview, Netanyahu warned that Israel could face international banking sanctions and said he had requested plans exploring alternative financial systems, including blockchain and cryptocurrencies. — link
